content.thinking: I should cite only directly observed evidence rather than candidate-derived figures, pulling from the actual trace entries like T5, T7, T9, T12, T17, T19, M1, and F1, and flagging F-rows as unverified. I'll avoid repeating specific timestamps and keep citations simple rather than referencing candidate-only figures.

action_items.item: Run the proposed autoscaling config test (scale-down window at least the Kubernetes default, minimum replicas not above maximum) in CI so it runs on every change to the values files. It has not been run yet.
Add an alert on the autoscaler changing replica count back and forth repeatedly within a short period, so flapping pages before or alongside the latency alert.
Once the scale-down window fix is merged and synced, decide whether to keep or lower the raised autoscaler floor, and verify that the replica count stays steady under the same traffic.

causal_chain.step: People using io-shop saw slow responses for {duration}. The tail latency the alert watches rose from {series_before} before onset to {series_while_broken} on average, peaking at {series_at_worst}. The error rate did not rise: {errors_while_broken} while broken against {errors_before} before.

The service had too little capacity for its traffic during the slow minutes. The service was running three replicas when the mitigation began. Raising the floor from {T19.2} to {T19.3} replicas made the paging rule stop firing, and the service was no longer at the incident's level.

The replica count did not stay at the higher level by itself. The Investigator's reading of the metrics showed the CPU limit moving between two values while traffic stayed steady. That reading is a hypothesis, but the confirmed mitigation fits it: pinning the floor at the higher count ended the slow period.

The controller was set to act on every reading. Code-Fix's reading of the source shows the scale-down stabilization window in deploy/values-production.yaml is {F1.6}. At the higher replica count, load spreads out and per-replica CPU drops below the {F1.8} target, so the controller scales back down. The lower count saturates CPU, latency rises, and the next scale-up follows. This is a reading of the source only and is unverified. Nothing ran it.

The record rules out other triggers. The read of production changes for the preceding day returned none, and the flag provider showed no recent flag changes. A rise in demand outgrowing fixed capacity was the alternative explanation, but it was never tried as a mitigation. The record does not show what made the flapping start when it did.

contributing_factors.factor: The scale-down window setting of zero reached production, and no check on the autoscaler settings was seen in the record. A test that would catch it was written only after the incident and has not been run.
Automatic sync of io-shop is off, so nothing merged reaches the service until it is turned back on. The permanent fix cannot reach production by merging alone.
No alert was seen for the replica count flapping. Detection relied on the latency alert, which by its rule waits {rule_waits} before it fires. Flapping would be visible earlier.
The mitigation, a raised autoscaler floor, hides the setting fault. It stays in place, and nothing records when to revisit it.

input.executive_summary: For a short stretch ({duration}) the shop responded much more slowly than usual. Latency for the slowest requests rose from {series_before} before onset to {series_while_broken} on average, and to {series_at_worst} at the worst point. The number of failed requests did not rise: the error rate was {errors_while_broken} against {errors_before} before. People using the shop saw slow pages rather than error pages. The service's capacity most likely kept bouncing between a lower and a higher level while traffic was steady. Argus raised the minimum capacity, which kept the service at the higher level, and the metrics returned to normal. A draft fix for the autoscaler setting that most likely caused the bouncing has been proposed and awaits review.

got_lucky: Error rate did not rise, so the harm was slowness and not failed requests.
The slow period was short and ended once the floor was raised.
went_well: The Investigator placed the onset in the metrics and noticed the capacity moving between two values.
The mitigation was confirmed by the metrics: the paging rule stopped firing after the floor was raised.
Code-Fix traced the flapping to a specific setting in the repo and proposed a draft fix with a test.
went_wrong: The fix has not been merged, and automatic sync is off, so the root fault remains in the config and the raised floor is the only protection.
The Investigator did not read logs, and the record shows no direct check of the controller's scaling decisions. The mechanism rests on a source reading.
The proposed test was not run, since no test runner was available.

input.root_cause: The io-shop autoscaler flapped between a low and a high replica count because its scale-down stabilization window was set to zero in deploy/values-production.yaml. At the higher count, per-replica CPU fell below target and the controller scaled straight back down. At the lower count CPU saturated and tail latency rose. This mechanism comes from Code-Fix's reading of the source. Nothing ran to verify it, so it is unverified.
input.symptom: Shop pages were slow, with no rise in errors
